name: bmad
description: 'Answers BMad questions and recommends the next skill from what is installed. Use when the user asks bmad for help, what to do next or where to start; to set up, update, repair, doctor, migrate or check the status of the installation, or add modules; or to see or change the active initiative.'

name: bmad-advanced-elicitation
description: 'Pushes a draft off its first answer with critique methods and proposes one revision. Use when the user or another skill names bmad-advanced-elicitation, or the user says "advanced elicitation". Not for a critique or a named method such as pre-mortem without that name.'

name: bmad-agent-analyst
description: Business analyst for market research, competitive analysis, and requirements. Use when the user asks to talk to Mary or requests the business analyst

name: bmad-agent-architect
description: System architect and technical design leader. Use when the user asks to talk to Winston or requests the architect

name: bmad-agent-dev
description: Senior software engineer who implements stories and code changes. Use when the user asks to talk to Amelia or requests the developer agent

name: bmad-agent-pm
description: Product manager for PRD creation and requirements discovery. Use when the user asks to talk to John or requests the product manager

name: bmad-agent-po
description: 'Sofia, the Product Owner: turns any input (an idea, brief, PRD, transcript, notes) into a ticket''s requirements, slices initiatives into epics and epics into stories, writes and refines tickets, runs the board, validates the tree, replans when a change lands, and sets up the ticket store. Use when the user asks for Sofia or the product owner, or says ''create a spec'', ''distill this PRD'', ''write the initiative from'', ''slice this'', ''split this epic'', ''break this into stories'', ''make a ticket'', ''refine this ticket'', ''what''s ready'', ''status of'', ''publish'', ''validate these tickets'', ''this changed, what now'', ''set up the ticket store''.'

name: bmad-agent-ux-designer
description: UX designer and UI specialist. Use when the user asks to talk to Sally or requests the UX designer

name: bmad-architecture
description: 'Work out and record the architecture decisions that keep separately built parts of a system consistent, in a short architecture document. Creates, updates, or validates one; works from a ticket file, with an existing codebase or architecture document beside it. Use when the user says "create the architecture", "create technical architecture", "architecture spine", or "create a solution design"'

name: bmad-brainstorming
description: Facilitate a brainstorming session using diverse creative techniques. Use when the user says 'help me brainstorm' or 'help me ideate'

name: bmad-build
description: 'Implements a story, feature, or bug fix end to end: plan, code, review, verify. Use when the user hands one over and leaves the edits to you; a bare ticket id or link counts. Skip obvious, low-risk mechanical maintenance such as small ignore-file, typo-only, formatting-only, or configuration-hygiene edits. Explicit BMAD requests always qualify. Do not volunteer for user-directed interactive edits or version-control operations that only record existing work.'

name: bmad-build-auto
description: 'Implements one story, feature, or bug fix end to end without human interaction: plan, code, review, verify, report status. Use when invoked by name, usually by an orchestrator'

name: bmad-code-review
description: 'Review code changes with several independent reviewers in parallel, then triage and present the findings. Use when the user says "run code review" or "review this code"'

name: bmad-customize
description: Authors and updates customization overrides for installed BMad skills. Use when the user says 'customize bmad', 'override a skill', 'change agent behavior', or 'customize a workflow'

name: bmad-deep-recon
description: 'Decision-grade research on a topic or this repository. Use when the user says "deep recon", "research this", "draft a research prompt", "process this research report", "market research", "domain research", "technical research", "competitor research", "what users say about X", "literature review", "help me choose between", "research the codebase", "research how X works here" or "why is X built this way". Not for a quick code question answered in chat.'

name: bmad-eval
description: 'Runs the evals of a BMad skill through the agent harness the user works in and reports what they show: baseline against the bare model, variant against a stripped or prior version, quality against a rubric, and trigger accuracy of the description with an optional optimization loop. Use when the user asks to evaluate, benchmark, test the triggers of, grade, or compare versions of a skill, or when the bmad-toolsmith skill asks for an eval of a skill it built.'

name: bmad-facilitate
description: 'Coaches the user through writing, updating or validating a document. Use when invoked by skill name only'

name: bmad-forge-idea
description: Test a half-formed idea in a questioning conversation, with different personas probing its weak points, until the user can act on it or drop it with confidence. Optionally writes a short brief for planning skills to build on. Use when the user says 'forge an idea', 'pressure-test this idea', 'stress-test my thinking', or 'harden this idea'

name: bmad-ingest
description: 'Turns a transcript, thread, voice memo or long document into a cited note agents can act on. Use when the user says "ingest this", "process this transcript", "make notes from this thread or recording" or "what came out of this meeting".'

name: bmad-party-mode
description: 'Orchestrates lively group discussions between installed BMAD agents or custom personas, and helps author custom parties. Use when the user requests party mode, a roundtable, or multiple agent perspectives — or wants to create/configure a party, define personas, or build an AI focus-group panel'

name: bmad-prd
description: Create, update, or validate a PRD. Use when the user wants help producing, editing, or validating a PRD

name: bmad-prfaq
description: "Test a product concept with Amazon's Working Backwards method: write the press release for the finished product first, then answer hard customer and stakeholder questions, ending in a complete PRFAQ document. Use when the user requests to 'create a PRFAQ', 'work backwards', or 'run the PRFAQ challenge'"

name: bmad-product-brief
description: Create, update, or validate a product brief. Use when the user wants help producing, editing, or validating a brief

name: bmad-project-context
description: 'Set up, adopt, refresh, or audit a repository''s agent instructions (the AGENTS.md block) so AI agents work well in that repo. Also records observed agent mistakes as pitfalls. Use when invoked by name'

name: bmad-qa-generate-e2e-tests
description: 'Add end-to-end and API tests for features that already work, following the project''s existing test harness. Use when the user asks for e2e tests, API tests, or automated coverage of an existing feature, or says "create qa automated tests for [feature]". Not for unit tests on work in flight, which the build writes.'

name: bmad-retrospective
description: 'Review a finished epic folder in the ticket tree against the evidence it left behind — the epic file, each ticket''s story file and plan, diffs, commits — and produce a retrospective with sourced findings, action items, and an acceptance decision. Use when the user says "run a retrospective" or "lets retro the epic [epic]". Supports -H/--headless'

name: bmad-review
description: 'Runs one or more installed review lenses — adversarial critique, edge cases, verification gaps, structure, prose — and reports triaged findings. Use when, and only when, the user asks you to review a diff, a pull request, or an artifact — code or documents, one or many — and actually says "review"; an explicit skill:bmad-review directive from another skill counts as that ask. A request to act on feedback from an earlier review is a change, not a review. Never invoke this uninvited, including on edits you just made.'

name: bmad-shard-pro
description: 'Makes long documents easy for agents to navigate. Use when the user says "shard this document", "this file is too long for agents", "turn this document into a wiki", "add a table of contents so agents can find things", or "update the sharded document".'

name: bmad-toolsmith
description: 'Smithy the Toolsmith builds and maintains BMad skills, agents and modules. Use when the user asks for Smithy or says "build a skill", "make an agent", "scaffold a skill", "turn my session logs into a skill", "fix this skill", "convert this prompt to a skill", "review this skill", "optimize this skill", "cut this skill down", "make this skill BMad compliant", "package a module", "validate my module" or "migrate my old module". Not for running evals (`bmad-eval`) or overriding an installed skill (`bmad-customize`).'

name: bmad-ux
description: 'Capture the user''s UX vision in two documents: DESIGN.md for how the product looks and EXPERIENCE.md for how it behaves. Use when the user says "lets create UX design" or "create UX specifications" or "help me plan the UX"'

name: bmad-walkthrough
description: 'Guide a human review of a commit, PR, file, or directory. Use when invoked by name'
